gloss: hands-on father; dad who is active in childcare

definitions.gloss: hands-on father; dad active in childcare
definitions.explanation: A father who is actively involved in raising his children, doing tasks traditionally associated with mothers in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧イクメンで、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦{保育園|ほいくえん}→保育園：04704_hoikuen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{送|おく}り{迎|むか}え→送り迎え：14362_okurimukae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He's a hands-on dad who takes his kid to and from daycare every day.

examples.japanese: イクメン⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えて→増える：01183_fueru⟧きた⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It's said that hands-on dads are increasing.

examples.japanese: イクメン⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{目指|めざ}して→目指す：10528_mezasu⟧⟦{育児|いくじ}{休暇|きゅうか}→育児休暇：07143_ikujikyuuka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}った→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: I took parental leave, aiming to be a hands-on dad.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
A blend of ⟦{育児|いくじ}→育児：03998_ikuji⟧ (childcare) and the ending of ⟦イケメン→イケメン：04761_ikemen⟧ (good-looking guy), which supplies the trendy "-メン" ending.
Popularized in the late 2000s as part of government campaigns to encourage fathers to participate more in childcare. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare launched the イクメンプロジェクト in 2010.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese society, childcare was primarily the mother's responsibility. The イクメン movement encourages fathers to take a more active role. The term reflects changing gender roles in Japan, though some criticize it for making basic parenting seem exceptional.
